title: Fasting, prayer, and almsgiving need one another
english: And how can we lay hold of the crown? Fasting is good, but without prayer it does not trample on demons. For he says, “This kind does not go out except by fasting and prayer” (Mark 9:29). Prayer is good too, but without almsgiving it cannot go up to heaven. You have heard the angel saying to Cornelius, “Your prayers and your almsgiving have gone up for a memorial before God” (Acts 10:4). So almsgiving carried prayer up to heaven.
translator_notes: The Greek text may be a fragment, and the translation is literal; no words were added or invented to complete the sentences.
baehrens: PG 93; In sanctos martyres (Khazarzar) u01 rem early
orientation: The preacher is showing that each virtue is powerless without another, beginning with fasting, prayer, and almsgiving.

title: Each virtue needs its companion
english: Almsgiving, then, is wonderful, but without faith it does not work redemption from sins. For he says, "By almsgiving and faith sins are cleansed." Gentleness is something to be zealous for, but without humility it cannot produce a royal character. For the Lord says, "Learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart" (Matthew 11:29). Faith is good, since even the smallest measure of it can move mountains, but without love it is vain and superfluous. For he says, "Even if I have faith so as to move mountains, but do not have love, I am nothing" (1 Corinthians 13:2).
translator_notes: The final clause is incomplete due to the source being cut off, and the ending is implied but not explicitly stated.
baehrens: PG 93; In sanctos martyres (Khazarzar) u01 rem mid
orientation: The preacher continues his chain of paired virtues, now showing that almsgiving needs faith, gentleness needs humility, and faith needs love.

title: Pursue all virtues together
english: So then, beloved, let us be eager to pursue these virtues, so that we may be counted worthy of the kingdom of heaven. Do not be zealous about faith, beloved, yet more sluggish about zeal itself; do not be hardworking about the Scriptures, yet unphilosophical about your character. For you must be rich in good works, in word, in wisdom, in self-control, in righteousness, in courage, in piety, in prudence, and in holiness. For just as wickedness punishes those who pursue it even before hell, so virtue makes those who work at it feast in delight even before the kingdom.
translator_notes: The Greek text may be a fragment, as it begins with a sentence that seems to be a conclusion or a wish, rather than a complete thought.
baehrens: PG 93; In sanctos martyres (Khazarzar) u01 rem close
orientation: The preacher is closing his address to the congregation, urging them to pursue all the virtues he has just discussed so that they may be counted worthy of the kingdom of heaven.
